approach: Fix the ordering at the plan sort in plan.rs. Add `Plan::build_improving`, which wraps `build_capped`. It first raises an improvement request whose cause is recorded in 3 or more distinct jobs to urgent, in memory and never for a person-set item. Then it walks the whole order once with a gap rule: never more than two non-improvement dispatches in a row while a ready improvement item is queued. Where a third non-improvement item would come next, the best-ranked ready improvement item moves into that slot. Every such slot is recorded in `Plan.turns`, so the plan shows every turn and a drain replan reproduces the rest. An improvement request is identified from recorded links by a pure athena-core function `hestia::improvement_of(records)`. The set is the open steward-channel requests (`steward::improvement_requests`) plus the open request that `repeated_causes` links to each repeated cause (`RepeatedCause.request`). Hestia files on channel `cli`, so the link is the only way to find its requests; filing is unchanged. The distinct-job count is `RepeatedCause.jobs.len()`. The drain counts consecutive non-improvement dispatches (`since_turn`) so a replan keeps the gap. `athena plan` prints `turn` and `promoted` lines, and the drain report lists the turns actually taken.

decisions.choice: Identify improvement requests with `hestia::improvement_of(&Records) -> Improvement` in hestia.rs. Its items are the open steward-channel jobs plus every open `RepeatedCause.request.job` from `repeated_causes`. `cause_jobs[job]` is the largest `RepeatedCause.jobs.len()` of a cause the job addresses. `RealSteps::improvement` is a one-line call.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 3. Only `RequestQueue::apply` writes channel `steward` (steward.rs:654). Every Hestia filing path calls `Athena::queue`, which writes channel `cli` (reading.rs:878-896; hestia.rs:749, 1662, 1803, 1993, 2001, 2071), so a channel marker misses Hestia. `repeated_causes` already links each cause to the open request citing its introspections (hestia.rs:277-319, 373-380) and counts distinct jobs (hestia.rs:355-363). Making the derivation pure lets one test cover the path from records to the `Improvement` input.

rejected.option: Mark improvement requests by channel `steward` alone
rejected.why: Misses every Hestia request, which is filed on channel `cli`.

rejected.option: Match request titles such as 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure'
rejected.why: Fragile text matching; the recorded cause link already exists.

rejected.option: A `cause_jobs_cited` substring helper over the request text
rejected.why: The cause-to-request link and the job count are already computed by `repeated_causes`; a second text match would duplicate `addressing_request` (hestia.rs:292).

rejected.option: Change how Hestia files (a channel or marker on its requests)
rejected.why: Out of scope: filing must not change.

decisions.choice: The slot rule is a gap rule over the whole order. Walk the untried positions with `gap = min(since_turn, 2)`. An improvement item resets gap to 0. At a non-improvement item with gap 2, move the first later improvement item that is untried and ready into that position. Ready means every in-plan dependency is tried or sits at an index before the slot. Record each item that sits in a gap-2 slot, moved or already there, as an `ImprovementTurn { id, position, moved }`. An improvement item that sits earlier at gap below 2 is not a turn. A candidate that is not ready is skipped, and the next position is retried.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. One pass over the whole order means `athena plan` shows every turn. After each dispatch the drain replans with `since_turn` advanced, and the same walk gives the same remaining order, so first-plan order equals dispatch order. A sliding gap of at most two also satisfies 'at least one in every three dispatches' for overlapping windows, which fixed non-overlapping windows would not. Tiers and groups stay intact apart from the moved items.

rejected.option: Move one item in the first window only (the previous design)
rejected.why: The printed plan lists one turn where the drain will take several, and it differs from the drain's real order.

rejected.option: A stateless rule that places an improvement item at index 2 on every build
rejected.why: The drain rebuilds before each wave (drain.rs:2986-2990), so the item would be pushed back each time and starve.

rejected.option: Interleave the whole order, every third entry
rejected.why: Reshuffles tiers and groups; the gap rule moves only items that are due.

rejected.option: Mark every dispatched improvement item as a turn
rejected.why: An item that ranked early on its own did not need the guarantee.

decisions.choice: Groups are rebuilt after the moves. A new group starts where the original group differs from the previous item's, and also before and after each moved turn item, which becomes a singleton. The result is subsets of the original disjoint groups, so grouping stays valid.
decisions.reason: A wave under `drain_concurrent` dispatches a whole group. A moved item in its own group means the group before it holds at most two items, so the one-in-three share holds per item and not only per wave.

rejected.option: Leave the groups as `build_with` made them
rejected.why: A group of six disjoint urgent items would dispatch together ahead of the improvement item.

decisions.choice: The urgent promotion is applied in memory before `build_capped`, only to improvement items that are not person-set and are below urgent, when `cause_jobs >= REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS` (3, a new constant in plan.rs). It is recorded as `RepeatPromotion { id, jobs, from }` in `Plan.promoted`. `athena plan` prints the later demotion beside the promotion when `Plan.demoted` shows the item was demoted from urgent.
decisions.reason: Caps and person-set semantics stay as they are (out of scope), and the maintainer sees both facts together (finding 5). A person's priority is never lowered or raised. `hestia::REPEAT_JOBS` (2, the filing threshold) is untouched.

rejected.option: Promote after the caps so promoted items are exempt
Write the promoted priority to a record
rejected.why: Not requested; keeps records and the round-trip test unaffected.
Out of scope: it would change when root-cause requests are filed.

decisions.choice: `Plan::priority_violations` skips a moved turn item when it looks for the earlier, worse-priority item. `prepare` turns each violation into a 'plan order contradicts priority' note (drain.rs:2202-2204), so every guaranteed turn would otherwise print a false note.
decisions.reason: The check belongs with the ordering rule.

rejected.why: Duplicates the knowledge of who was moved.

decisions.choice: `Plan::build_improving` is a new function that wraps `build_capped`. With no improvement item among the entries it returns exactly the `build_capped` result. `Drain::prepare` is the only caller changed. No field is added to `PlanEntry`.
decisions.reason: Existing `build_with` and `build_capped` callers and tests stay untouched, and criterion 3 is shown by equality with `build_capped`. `PlanEntry` is built by struct literal in many places and the flag is meaningful only to the drain.

rejected.why: Touches every struct literal in plan.rs, drain.rs unit tests and tests/drain.rs.

decisions.choice: The drain tracks `since_turn` (consecutive non-improvement dispatches) and `improvement_turns` in `State`. After `tried.extend` in `drain_with`, a `note_dispatch(&wave, &plan)` call updates `since_turn` per item, in wave order. It copies into `Report.improvement_turns` each dispatched id that is in `plan.turns` of the plan it was dispatched from. A new default method `Steps::improvement()` returns an empty `Improvement`, so existing doubles compile unchanged.
decisions.reason: The plan shows the turns planned and the report shows the turns taken, from the same rule. Unplanned items still advance `since_turn`.

rejected.why: Misses Hestia and would count items that did not need the guarantee.

decisions.choice: No refusal or matching rule is added, so no refusal_corpus case is mapped. Items are matched by recorded fields and by the existing `addressing_request` citation rule, which is read, not changed. The change reorders ready work and refuses no reading, so no refusal-rate figure is needed.
decisions.reason: Nothing parsed from text is added; `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is not a demonstration, because no reading, stem or stop-list code is touched.

rejected.why: The corpus covers readings and request-text parsing, and none of those paths changes.

Call `build_capped` on the copies. risks.risk: The promotion happens before `[priority_caps]`, so a promoted request is demoted to high when person-set urgent items fill the urgent tier. 'Treated as urgent' then holds only when there is room.
risks.mitigation: The guaranteed turn does not depend on priority, so the request still runs within three dispatches. `athena plan` prints the promotion and the demotion together, a plan.rs test covers it, and the CHANGELOG states the limit. Changing the caps is out of scope.

risks.risk: Moving an item could put a dependent before what it needs, or break a disjoint group.
risks.mitigation: A candidate moves only when every in-plan dependency is tried or sits before the target slot. Splitting a group only makes subsets of a disjoint group. A test checks every dependency precedes its dependent on the moved plan.

risks.risk: A person's own request that cites an introspection id of a repeated cause is treated as an improvement request, because Hestia requests are found by their link to the cause, not by author.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: this is the existing meaning of 'addresses a cause' in `addressing_request`. A person-set priority is never changed and the request gets only its share of turns. The CHANGELOG says 'the open request that cites the cause's introspections'. A test covers a request citing nothing (not listed).

risks.risk: `repeated_causes` is O(introspections x groups) and runs on each replan.
risks.mitigation: A request is listed only when `repeated_causes` links it, and only open requests are listed. `improvement_of` runs once per `prepare`. The test files a request through the real `error_review_backfill`.

risks.risk: `batches_for` puts items with no plan entry ahead of planned ones (drain.rs 2843-2853), so a few dispatches can precede the improvement turn.
risks.mitigation: Items with no plan entry still advance `since_turn`, so the next planned dispatch is the improvement item. The case already exists and is unchanged.

risks.risk: Under `drain_concurrent` a whole group dispatches at once, which could dilute the one-in-three share.
risks.mitigation: Moved turn items are singleton groups, and a `drain_concurrent` test checks the first wave.

risks.risk: A tried item that stays in the queue (failed or held) could distort the gap count.
risks.mitigation: The walk runs over the untried positions only, and `tried` items stay in place and are ignored. A test with a tried improvement item shows it is neither counted nor moved.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in plan.rs build 8 entries: six `Priority::Urgent` person-filed ids and two `Priority::Normal` Steward ids, with dependencies and touches empty. Case A uses `TierCaps::UNLIMITED`. Case B uses `TierCaps { urgent: 3, high: 10 }` with the six ids in `person_set`, so all six stay urgent as person-set items are never demoted. `Plan::build_improving` gets `Improvement { items: [s1, s2], since_turn: 0, .. }`. Further cases: `since_turn` 2 puts an improvement item first; `since_turn` 1 puts it at the second position; a tried improvement item is not counted. A walk test builds the plan from the full order, then simulates the drain by removing the first dispatched id and rebuilding with the advanced `since_turn` and tried set, for 8 dispatches, and asserts the concatenated dispatch order equals the first build's `order`.
demonstrations.observes: `plan.order[..3]` contains a Steward id, in case A and case B. `plan.turns` names both Steward ids, at positions 3 and 6 (1-based) with `moved: true`. The same inputs through `Plan::build_capped` leave both Steward ids last. The simulated dispatch order equals the first plan's order. No two consecutive turns have more than two non-improvement ids between them.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the gap rule the order is the six urgent ids and then both Steward ids, so the first-three assertion fails. Without `since_turn`, the drain-level test in criterion 4 fails because the item is pushed back on each replan.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Plan::build_improving` (added by step 2). The `Improvement` value is a plain argument and no double is used. Plan entries are built with the struct-literal helper that the existing plan.rs tests use (exists). Nothing under test is inside a fixture.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (a) hestia.rs `improvement_of` tests use the existing harness `athena_in`, `class`, `introspection` and `put` (hestia.rs:2508-2567). They commit a failure class with introspections for jobs a, b, c, plus a failure-class cause with only jobs a, b for the companion. The request is filed through the real Hestia path, `athena.error_review_backfill` (the tests at hestia.rs:3630-3712 call it), so it lands on channel `cli` through `Athena::queue`. A second case queues, with `athena.queue`, a request that cites the introspection ids. `improvement_of(&records(&athena))` must list that job with `cause_jobs == 3`; with two jobs it lists it with 2. A plain `athena.queue` person request citing nothing is not listed. A steward-channel request, built as a `Request` with channel `steward` the way the fixture at hestia.rs:3354 is, is listed with 0. A request closed by `athena close` is not listed. (b) plan.rs `repeat_urgent` tests pass `Improvement { cause_jobs: {h: 3} }` and an older normal entry to `build_improving`. The returned entries show `h` at Urgent and `plan.promoted` holds `{jobs: 3, from: Normal}` with `h` ordered first. The 2-job case leaves it normal, `promoted` empty, and the order by age. A `person_set` item is not promoted. With the urgent tier full of three person-set items, a promoted item is demoted to high and shows in both `plan.promoted` and `plan.demoted`.

(b) An improvement entry depends on a job that `history` shows failed with no landed retry; it is held, in `refused`. (e) A moved turn item produces no `priority_violations` entry.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0, including `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (no prompt or brief text changes).
demonstrations.fails_without: A new `Steps` method, `Plan` field, `Report` field or `State` field that is not wired through the struct literals (the `Report` literal at drain.rs:3057 and the `State` literal in `Drain::new`) would not compile or would fail clippy.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo toolchain over the whole workspace; it exists.

demonstrations.method: Read the new entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` and match each sentence to the diff. The entry states: the root cause (the drain ordered by person-set priority alone); the guaranteed turn (at most two other dispatches between improvement requests while a ready one is queued, for open steward-channel requests and for the open request that addresses a repeated cause); the raise to urgent for a cause recorded in three or more distinct jobs, made before `[priority_caps]` so a full urgent tier can demote it again, and never applied to a priority a person set; the `turn` and `promoted` lines in `athena plan`; the improvement line in the drain report; the new `Steps::improvement` method.
demonstrations.observes: Every sentence maps to a changed function or test, and nothing is claimed about the filing threshold, Hestia or Steward text, or caps.
demonstrations.fails_without: An entry that claimed more than the diff (for example a change to the filing threshold or to the caps) would not map to a changed function or test.
demonstrations.seam: Not a test; a reading of the diff by the verifier with `git diff`.

demonstrations.method: List the changed paths and compare them with the deliverables.
demonstrations.observes: Only crates/athena-core/src/{plan,hestia,steward}.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/{drain,display,main}.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed. athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows are not touched.
demonstrations.fails_without: A changed athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow would show in the listed paths.
demonstrations.seam: Not a test; `git status` over the working tree.
